intended_object: The degree-n homogeneous component Sym^n(M) of the symmetric algebra Sym_R(M) over a commutative semiring R, seen as a submodule of the algebra. It is the R-span of all products of n elements of M. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `LinearMap.range (SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M) ^ n`. Here `Submodule` power is the iterated submodule product: the span of products of n elements of ι(M). This is exactly the image of M^{⊗n} in Sym(M), which is the standard degree-n component.

The case n = 0 is also right. There `^ 0` gives `1 : Submodule`, which is the range of `algebraMap R`, i.e. the scalars, the correct degree-0 part.

Mathlib uses the same pattern to grade `TensorAlgebra` and `ExteriorAlgebra`, via `LinearMap.range (ι R) ^ n`. The library uses this definition to build a `GradedAlgebra` instance, which also certifies that the components form a direct-sum decomposition. It also proves that the components match the homogeneous polynomials under a basis presentation.

The generality is natural: any commutative semiring R and any module M, with no basis or freeness needed.

Mathlib has `SymmetricPower R n M`, but that is a standalone quotient type, not a submodule of `SymmetricAlgebra`. Mathlib does not grade `SymmetricAlgebra`, so there is no exact counterpart.
